Frequently asked questions

How do I preview a PBR material?

Drop the texture files for one material into the viewer together. Choose a sphere to see how highlights follow a curved surface, or a plane to inspect the texture as it tiles. Switch lighting presets to compare the same material under different lights.

Which texture maps can I use?

Load base color, normal, roughness, metallic, ambient occlusion, height, emissive, opacity, glossiness, and specular maps. The viewer matches filenames such as stone_roughness.png automatically. If a file is unmatched, use the menu beside its name to assign it.

How do I load a packed ORM, ARM, RMA, or MRA map?

Include the layout in the filename, for example stone_orm.png. Each layout assigns a material property to the red, green, and blue channels in this order:

  • ORM / ARM — ambient occlusion, roughness, metallic
  • RMA — roughness, metallic, ambient occlusion
  • MRA — metallic, roughness, ambient occlusion
Why do bumps look like dents?

Check the normal map convention. Enable DirectX normal map (flip green) for a DirectX map. Leave it off for an OpenGL map.

How can I see what a single map contributes?

Click the green check beside a loaded map to turn it off. Click the minus to turn it back on. The texture stays loaded, so you can compare both views under the same lighting.

Do my textures leave my device?

Your browser reads the texture files locally and renders the material with WebGL. To save a PNG of the current view, use the Save preview image button in the preview.
